caveat: kUSD is TN10 research software: not audited, not a product, not for real value.

timeline.note: No refresh for over an hour, so anyone froze the oracle; consumers stopped minting.
kUSD redeemed for KAS through the PSM, fee paid to the surplus pot.

After a simulated crash (raw price 8000 → 2000) the liquidation price fell at most 25% per hour; three hours later the vault was liquidated at 2532 in one atomic transaction, with the penalty split between the keeper and the surplus pot.
Governance spent from the surplus pot (2 of 3 signatures).
The liquidated vault closed and its remaining 2.97 KAS of collateral was released.
Oracle created with five operator slots (on TN10 all five keys are held by the deployer), starting at 40 cents per KAS.
Peg stability module created (KAS in, kUSD out), not yet wired to the token.
Surplus pot created; fees and liquidation penalties land here.
Issuance budget created: at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day.
kUSD token authority created; it mints only for covenants it knows by template.
PSM wired to the token authority.
Issuance budget wired in; every mint now draws from it.
First collateral vault opened: 10 KAS locked.
Price refreshed from three separately signed prints: operators 0, 2 and 4 printed 4100 / 4120 / 4090, median $0.4100. The relayer can't change the price, and no operator signed the transaction.
Out-of-band prints 4100 / 4110 / 4600: spread over 3%, refused by the covenant (never broadcast).
Operator slot 4 rotated to a fresh key, signed by operators 0, 1 and 2 (never by the slot being replaced).
Refresh using the new slot-4 key: operators 1, 3 and 4 printed 4150 / 4140 / 4160, median $0.4150. The mint price moved only 4100 → 4108 because of the rate limit.
Governance (2 of 3) lowered the daily issuance limit from $50,000 to $40,000.
Minted $2.00 of kUSD against the vault, priced at the rate-limited mint price ($0.4108), not the raw $0.4150.
Routine refresh after the feed went stale: operators 0, 2 and 3 printed 4160 / 4150 / 4170, median $0.4160. The mint price caught up 4108 → 4160, within its 10%-per-hour limit.
Repaid the $2.00 in full before switching to real prices (the burn credits the issuance budget back); the vault stayed open with 10 KAS.

Switched from test prints to the real KAS price: operators 2, 3 and 4 each printed CoinGecko's KAS/USD, 258 ($0.0258). The mint price followed at once; the liquidation price can only fall 25% per hour, so it walks down over about half a day.
Deposited 290 KAS more, so the vault stays healthy at the real KAS price.
Deposited 1 KAS more and topped up the box's fee headroom (it pays a mint's dust and fee).
Minted $2.00 of kUSD again at the real price ($0.0258): 301 KAS of collateral, worth $7.77, is 388% of the debt (minimum 175%).
Retiring this deployment: repaid the $2.00 and withdrew all 301 KAS of collateral.
Closed the empty vault and released its last 0.9 KAS; this deployment is retired.

Oracle created with five operator slots (on TN10 all five keys are held by the deployer), starting at the real KAS price, 262 ($0.0262). In this deployment every clock is proven by the transaction's lock time, so no step needs a freshly confirmed input.
Peg stability module created (KAS in, kUSD out), not yet wired to the token.
Surplus pot created; fees and liquidation penalties land here.
Issuance budget created: at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day.
kUSD token authority created; it mints only for covenants it knows by template.
PSM wired to the token authority.
Issuance budget wired in; every mint now draws from it.
Collateral vault opened: 300 KAS locked.
First refresh with a lock-time clock: operators 0, 2 and 4 each printed CoinGecko's KAS/USD, 262 ($0.0262), signed at the transaction's own lock time. No funding transaction had to confirm first.

The same refresh claiming a clock five minutes ahead: the covenant's own check passed, but the node refused the transaction as not final, because its lock time hadn't been reached. Nobody can claim time that hasn't passed.
Minted $2.00 of kUSD at $0.0262: 300 KAS of collateral, worth $7.86, is 393% of the debt (minimum 175%). The vault and the issuance budget read the same lock-time clock.
Out-of-band prints 262 / 263 / 290: spread over 3%, refused by the covenant (never broadcast).
Operator slot 4 rotated to a fresh key, signed by operators 0, 1 and 2 (never by the slot being replaced).
Refresh using the new slot-4 key: operators 1, 3 and 4 each printed 262 ($0.0262).
Swapped KAS for $1.00 of kUSD through the peg module at the mint price, in a transaction built by kusd-client, the library the browser app runs.
Redeemed that $1.00 of kUSD for KAS through the peg module at the liquidation price (also built by kusd-client).
Retiring the 175% vault before the liquidation line moved: repaid the $2.00 and withdrew all 300 KAS.
Closed the empty vault and released its last 0.9 KAS.
Liquidation line moved to 150% (borrowing still stops at 175%): the vault code changed, so a new peg stability module was created beside the same oracle and surplus pot.
New issuance budget for the 150% deployment: at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day.
New kUSD token authority that knows the 150% vault: vaults now become liquidatable only below 150% of their debt, while borrowing still stops at 175%.
New PSM wired to the new token authority.
New issuance budget wired in.
Collateral vault opened under the 150% liquidation line: 300 KAS locked.
Minted $2.00 of kUSD from the new vault at $0.0270: 300 KAS, worth $8.10, is 405% of the debt (borrowing stops at 175%, liquidation below 150%). It used the same oracle box as before.
Governance (2 of 3) set the new PSM's ceiling to $50,000 and its fee to 0.50%, as before.
Liquidation rehearsal: a second vault opened with 20 KAS.
Rehearsal vault topped up to 65.5 KAS.
Rehearsal vault borrowed $1.00 at $0.0270: 65.5 KAS, worth $1.77, is 176% of the debt, just over the 175% borrowing line and 26 points above the liquidation line.
Rehearsal price drop: operators 0, 1 and 2 printed 251. The mint price followed at once; the liquidation price may fall only 25% per hour, so it stopped at 260, leaving the vault at 170%.

Liquidation attempted with the vault at 170% at the liquidation price ($0.0260): refused by the covenant (never broadcast). Under the old shared 175% line this vault would already have been liquidatable.
Half an hour later operators 2, 3 and 4 printed 225 and the liquidation price reached it: the vault fell to 147%, under the 150% line.

The price fell to $0.0225 and the vault sat at 147%, under the 150% line: liquidated in one transaction. The keeper burned the $1.00 debt and took 48.89 KAS (110%), the surplus pot took 1.33 KAS (3%), and 16.28 KAS stayed with the vault's owner.
Closed the liquidated vault; the owner got its remaining 16.18 KAS back.
Retiring the 150% deployment's vault before the surge-fee change: repaid the $2.00 and withdrew all 300 KAS.
Closed the empty vault and released its last 0.9 KAS.

The PSM's buy fee now rises as the day's issuance budget empties (0.50% while at least half is left, up to 2.50% at empty), and a vault with debt must hold at least 5 KAS, enough to pay a full liquidation: both change covenant code, so a new PSM was created beside the same oracle and surplus pot.
New issuance budget for the surge-fee deployment: at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day; the buy fee rises once half of it is gone.
New kUSD token authority that knows the 5 KAS vault and the surge-fee PSM.
Surge-fee PSM wired to the new token authority.
New issuance budget wired in.
Collateral vault opened in the surge-fee deployment: 300 KAS locked (the minimum is now 5 KAS).
Governance (2 of 3) set the surge-fee PSM's ceiling to $50,000 and its base fee to 0.50%.
Minted $2.00 of kUSD from the surge-fee deployment's vault at $0.0268: 300 KAS, worth $8.04, is 402% of the debt. A vault with debt now needs at least 5 KAS, enough to pay a full liquidation.
Governance (2 of 3) cut the daily issuance budget to $4.00 for a live check of the rising buy fee.

Bought $3.00 of kUSD with the day's budget at $4.00: the first $2.00 paid the flat 0.50%, the last $1.00 paid a rate rising from 0.50% towards 2.50% as the budget emptied. The surplus pot received 0.746 KAS, 0.667% of the 111.9 KAS paid, exactly the covenant's figure (flat, it would have been 0.560 KAS).
Governance (2 of 3) restored the daily issuance budget to $50,000.
Retiring the surge-fee deployment's vault before the stability fee: repaid the $2.00 and withdrew all 300 KAS.
Closed the empty vault and released its last 0.9 KAS.
Oracle re-created with the stability-fee rate index: every refresh now also compounds a 2% a year interest index on its own signed clock, and governance can move the rate without a redeploy.

Stability fee: kUSD debt now accrues interest at a governance-set annual rate (2% at launch), paid in kUSD. The oracle, vault and token code changed, so a new PSM was created beside the same surplus pot.
New issuance budget for the stability-fee deployment: at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day.
New kUSD token authority that knows the interest-bearing vault; the interest borrowers pay accumulates here as the protocol's revenue.
Stability-fee PSM wired to the new token authority.
New issuance budget wired in.
Collateral vault opened in the stability-fee deployment: 300 KAS locked; its debt will accrue interest.
Governance (2 of 3) set the stability-fee PSM's ceiling to $50,000 and its base fee to 0.50%.
Minted $4.00 of kUSD from the stability-fee deployment's vault at $0.0268: 300 KAS, worth $8.04, is 201% of the debt. From the next oracle refresh the debt accrues interest at 2% a year.

Governance (2 of 3) armed a 50% a year stability fee. The next refresh still accrued its gap at 2% (+207 index units), then switched; the one after added +4,133 units in five minutes, 20x the step before.
Bought $4.01 of kUSD through the peg module: the $4.00 vault owed $4.01 after its first refresh, and a $4.00 box had just been refused for clearing it ("clearing the vault takes at least 401 cents").
Repaid the $4.00 vault in full with the $4.01 box: $4.00 of principal and one cent of interest burned into the token authority, the collateral kept. The protocol's first cent of credit revenue.
Governance (2 of 3) armed 2% a year again; the next refresh switched back.
Retiring the stability-fee deployment's vault before Stage 2c: closed and its 300 KAS released (its debt had already been repaid in full).

Oracle re-created for Stage 2c: once governance binds it to the MinerMedian box, every refresh is clamped to within 5% of the price Kaspa's miners voted in their blocks (a proven 6,000-block window), when that median is fresh and at least half the blocks voted. Born unbound, with the same five operators.
Stage 2c: the oracle can now be bound to the chain's miner median, so the oracle changed and a new PSM was created around it, beside the same surplus pot.
New issuance budget for the Stage 2c deployment: at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day.
New kUSD token authority pinned to the miner-bounded oracle; interest and fees accumulate here.
Stage 2c PSM wired to the new token authority.
New issuance budget wired in.
Collateral vault opened in the Stage 2c deployment: 300 KAS locked.
Governance (2 of 3) set the Stage 2c PSM's ceiling to $50,000 and its base fee to 0.50%.
Minted $4.00 of kUSD from the Stage 2c deployment's vault at about $0.027: 300 KAS is roughly 200% of the debt, accruing interest at 2% a year.
Governance (2 of 3) bound the oracle to the MinerMedian box: from here every refresh runs through the miner bound (fresh, participating median → clamp to ±5%; otherwise Stage 1, recorded).

Stage 2c, the bound on: the first refresh through refresh_bounded, co-spending the MinerMedian box. The operators' median sat inside the ±5% band around the miners' median, so it went through unchanged with bounded = 1 recorded.

Stage 2c, the clamp: our test miners voted a price 8% below the exchanges while the operators printed the honest spot price; the refresh was clamped to the miner median +5%. Pools alone cannot move the price further than that, and operators alone cannot move it past the miners.

Stage 2c, fail-open: with the prover stopped for over 45 minutes the miner median went stale, and the refresh fell back to the Stage 1 price with bounded = 0 recorded. Miner silence never freezes the feed.
Retiring the Stage 2c deploy vault before the vault-debt ceiling: bought $4.03 of kUSD through the old PSM to repay the $4.01 it owed, interest included.
Repaid the Stage 2c deploy vault in full with a $4.03 box (up to 5 cents over what is owed is accepted) and released its 300 KAS.
Closed the empty Stage 2c deploy vault.

Vault-debt ceiling: the issuance budget now counts the debt every vault has settled and caps the total, so the vault, PSM and budget code changed; a new PSM was created beside the same oracle and surplus pot.
New issuance budget with a vault-debt ceiling of $330,000, sized from KAS order-book depth so liquidations can't swamp the market; at most $50,000 of new kUSD per day.
New kUSD token authority that knows the 200% / 170% vault and the ceiling-aware PSM and budget.
New PSM wired to the new token authority.
New issuance budget wired in.
New deploy vault opened with 10 KAS, the driver's default.
Topped the new deploy vault up to 300 KAS.

A $3.80 mint against the $3.00 vault-debt ceiling, refused before signing: "the vault-debt ceiling leaves room for 300 cents". No transaction was sent.
Minted $3.00 against the new vault with the vault-debt ceiling at $3.00, filling it exactly.
Governance (2 of 3) restored the vault-debt ceiling to $330,000.

Hardened PSM: swap-ins stop at $1,000 plus 25% of vault debt, a short reserve pays every redeemer the same share instead of first come, first served, and anyone can top the reserve up.

Anyone may add KAS to the PSM's reserve: the deployer added 1 KAS. If the reserve is ever short, a top-up raises every remaining redemption at once.

Vault provenance: every vault is now opened by a vault factory, with zero debt, into the factory's covenant group, and the token authority accepts vaults only from that group. The token's config changed, so a new PSM was created beside the same oracle and surplus pot.

Cross-KCC-20 test: a token box created from kUSDT's own unmodified KCC-20 code (0.80 test units on TN10; a test instance, not kUSDT).
kUSD swapped for that kUSDT-code token in one transaction: each token's covenant checked only its own side, and neither side could land without the other.

An oracle with price receipts and operator pay, abandoned unused: its script held 24 signature checks and nodes relay only scripts with 15 or fewer, so it could never be spent. Replaced by the next one.

Oracle re-created with price receipts and operator pay: consumers read one of 8 receipt boxes instead of the oracle, so up to 8 users can act at once, and every price change replaces all of them (no stale price can be reused). Refreshes take 3 to 5 operator prints and use their median; each included print earns its operator 0.05 KAS, paid from the treasury on claim. One refresh entry, always bound to the miner median, keeps it under the 15-signature limit.
Governance (2 of 3) created the 8 price receipts, 10 KAS each.

Overflow fixes (formal/SPEC.md §8.4, §8.9): a new PSM whose redemptions are computed in 1e-4 KAS units, whose swap-ins are bounded by all the KAS that will ever exist, whose redemption fee no longer multiplies past 64 bits, and whose ceiling is capped at $40 billion.
